title: Nonblocking fallback cascade with compatibility quarantine and staggered regional retirement
creator: Marco Li
description:
Background: When customers pin a model version we guarantee exact-version routing for the pinned model. During capacity constraints, deprecation windows, or regional outages we must fall back without breaking contracts or silently changing semantics. Current fallback attempts are either too aggressive (surprising model swaps) or too conservative (requests fail instead of degrading).

Goal: Implement a nonblocking, observable fallback cascade for pinned versions that: 1) tries region-local compatible variants first, 2) isolates potentially incompatible variants in a short 'compatibility quarantine' where sampled traffic runs integration regressions, and 3) performs staggered regional retirement for deprecated pinned versions with explicit customer notifications and soft-grace periods.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Safety over cost: prefer to route to slightly older but compatibility-verified variants than to fail-open to an unverified faster variant. This increases unit cost in edge cases.
- Latency SLOs: prefer region-local fallbacks; only cross-region after local attempts fail.
- Operational complexity: quarantine adds orchestration and observability burden; we'll limit quarantine to short windows (5–15 minutes) and sampled traffic (0.5–2%).

Proposed design overview:
1) Fallback graph evaluated per-request with policy weights: local-pinned -> local-compatible-variant -> local-compatible-warm-variant -> quarantine-sampled-variant -> cross-region-compatible -> global-compat-variant -> fail.
2) Compatibility quarantine: when the system detects a potential variant with differing tokenizer or output-structure risk, we route a tiny sampled percentage to the variant and run server-side automated canary checks (structured-output tests, hallucination signals, latency regressions). Passing quarantine promotes the variant to broad routing for that pin.
3) Deprecation flow: owner-initiated deprecation schedules will trigger staggered regional retirement windows (region-by-region) with automated customer notifications and an enforced last-ditch fallback where we keep returning a 409 with deprecation-reason header for 48h before automatic substitution if customer opts out of auto-substitution.
4) Observability: expand Console to show per-pin fallback graph states, quarantine health metrics, and per-region failover counts.

Deliverables: design doc, runtime policy eval module, quarantine runner, console dashboard changes, alert rules, and migration script for existing pins.
acceptance_criteria: Fallback graph implemented in runtime and configurable via policy manifests
Compatibility quarantine can be enabled per-model and samples traffic at 0.5–2%
Console shows fallback counts and quarantine health for each pin
Automated canary checks detect structural incompatibilities (tokenizer mismatch, response schema deviations) and block promotion
Deprecation API supports staggered regional windows, customer notifications, and a 48h opt-out substitution window
Integration test suite with synthetic workloads demonstrates no increase in P95 latency beyond 10% for fallback cases
rollout_plan: Week 1: Ship policy framework and simple fallthrough (local -> cross-region) behind feature flag
Week 2: Implement quarantine sampler and basic canary checks; run on internal model pins (qa.redwood)
Week 3: Add Console views and alerting; onboard 3 pilot customers for pinned deprecated models
Week 4: Iterate on policy weights, safety thresholds; enable staged regional retirement flow for pilot customers
Week 5: Gradual ramp to all pinned models; disable feature flag after 95% rollout metrics pass
metrics: Fallback rate per pin (target: <1% for steady-state)
Quarantine sample health pass rate (target: >99% for promotion)
Pinned request success rate during deprecation windows (target: >99%)
Average P95 latency delta for requests that took a fallback path (target: <10%)
Number of unexpected semantic regressions detected post-promotion (target: 0 in first 24h)
